tasks.demo: See what it does in practice
tasks.quickstart: Install, run, play, or copy it
tasks.navigation: Find guides, support, or contribution paths
tasks.verification: Verify a claim about a release or revision
tasks.handoff: Hand the project to a maintainer or agent

records.title: Alternatives and tradeoffs
records.summary: Explain when a related tool or approach fits a reader better.
records.use_when: Two realistic options solve similar tasks with different costs or constraints.

records.title: Animated micro-demo
records.summary: Show a short interaction sequence that needs no narration.
records.use_when: The order of a short sequence is important to understanding it.

records.title: Annotated screenshot
records.summary: Identify the controls or evidence a reader needs to notice.
records.use_when: A useful screenshot has important controls or results that could be missed.

records.title: Architecture or flow diagram
records.summary: Show component relationships or the order of steps.
records.use_when: A system or workflow is hard to follow from prose alone.

records.title: Artifact verification instructions
records.summary: Explain how to compare a downloaded artifact with its recorded digest.
records.use_when: A downloadable artifact has a documented digest or signature.

records.title: Asset caption and provenance
records.summary: Name what a visual shows and identify its source or build where relevant.
records.use_when: A visual uses external work or needs version or authorship context.

records.title: Attribution and data provenance
records.summary: Link the source and terms for material external assets or datasets.
records.use_when: Documentation or examples rely on someone else’s data or assets.

records.title: Audience and use cases
records.summary: Name the people and jobs the project serves.
records.use_when: The project serves different roles or supports several jobs.

records.title: Benchmark method and scope
records.summary: Describe the workload, environment, revision, and units beside a performance result.
records.use_when: A performance number would be misleading without its workload or conditions.

records.title: Capabilities at a glance
records.summary: Show the few important things readers can do today.
records.use_when: A reader needs to compare major capabilities before installing.

records.title: Captioned video walkthrough
records.summary: Demonstrate a longer workflow with captions or a transcript.
records.use_when: A recording contains spoken directions or audible success cues.

records.title: Changelog and version navigation
records.summary: Show where release history lives and which version the reader is viewing.
records.use_when: Readers need to link product changes to a specific version.

records.title: Check keyboard navigation on the rendered README
records.summary: Use the keyboard on the published view to reach the primary links and any collapsible controls.
records.use_when: The rendered README has links or controls that readers navigate by keyboard.

records.title: Citation instructions
records.summary: Point researchers to the maintained citation metadata where appropriate.
records.use_when: Researchers need a maintained source for attributing a release.

records.title: Clean consumer adoption test
records.summary: Verify documented copy-in or install steps in a fresh consumer project.
records.use_when: Producer-local files or caches may hide problems in consumer adoption.

records.title: Cleanup or reset instructions
records.summary: Show how a reader can leave a temporary demo or restore a clean starting point.
records.use_when: A trial or setup leaves state readers may need to reset.

records.title: Clear heading hierarchy
records.summary: Organize sections in a predictable structure for visual scanning and assistive navigation.
records.use_when: The README has several sections or deeply nested material.

records.title: Combined-commit proof
records.summary: Tie a merge-readiness claim to tests on the exact combined content.
records.use_when: Changes were tested individually and also need integration evidence.

records.title: Concise comparison table
records.summary: Present repeated choices in a table when readers need to compare the same attributes.
records.use_when: Readers need to compare options on repeated criteria.

records.title: Consistent terms
records.summary: Use the same names for actions and objects as the code, UI, and linked instructions.
records.use_when: Several terms are used for the same concept across docs and UI.

records.title: Contribution route
records.summary: Point to contribution rules, issue templates, and where work is reviewed.
records.use_when: A new contributor needs the submission process and a first task.

records.title: Copy-in or template adoption path
records.summary: Identify what to copy, where it goes, and how to check the resulting project.
records.use_when: Adopters need to copy a small set of files into an existing checkout.

records.title: Describe what the installer changes
records.summary: Tell readers where binaries or files are installed, which persistent user settings change, and what supported option controls those changes.
records.use_when: Installation modifies files, configuration, or running services.

records.title: Descriptive link labels
records.summary: Use text that tells the reader where the link goes or what it does.
records.use_when: A generic link label would make the destination unclear out of context.

records.title: Developer entry point
records.summary: Link the source layout, setup, and shortest routine development check.
records.use_when: Development setup differs from ordinary installation or use.

records.title: Diagnostic decision guide
records.summary: Route different symptoms to the relevant fix instead of listing generic troubleshooting.
records.use_when: Similar errors require different checks or remedies.

records.title: Disclose telemetry defaults and controls
records.summary: Name the data a tool collects, the default participation state, and how to view or change the setting.
records.use_when: Installation or normal use can collect or transmit usage data.

records.title: Distinguish intended checks from results
records.summary: Show which checks were planned and which actually ran, with a scoped outcome for each.
records.use_when: A plan or checklist could be mistaken for the result of an executed check.

records.title: Distinguish source from the shipped product
records.summary: Explain what readers are browsing, which product or distribution it produces, and where each set of terms applies.
records.use_when: The source tree and the distributed product have different names, terms, or components.

records.title: Document automatic retry boundaries
records.summary: Tell automated readers which responses allow another attempt, which server signal controls the delay, and when retries should stop.
records.use_when: Transient failures are retried automatically and behavior depends on operation type.

records.title: Document the scripting interface
records.summary: Show where scripts can find structured output and which outcomes return which exit codes.
records.use_when: People or tools need to automate the task without parsing prose output.

records.title: Document what happens with concurrent writers
records.summary: Say which shared state is protected, when writers wait or fail, and whether the behavior depends on the storage backend or deployment mode.
records.use_when: Several processes can change the same state or use the same workspace.

records.title: Draft, archive, and publication stages
records.summary: Keep proposed text, frozen snapshots, and the published default-branch README distinguishable.
records.use_when: Proposed, frozen, and published README versions coexist.

records.title: Execute the documented walkthrough
records.summary: Replay the reader’s published steps at the named revision and verify the result.
records.use_when: A reader needs to know whether the written steps worked at the revision in view.

records.title: Expected output contract
records.summary: Separate stable result fields from variable example values when exact comparison matters.
records.use_when: A command or API produces output readers or scripts need to recognize.

records.title: Explain defaults that change what readers see
records.summary: Name the input the tool omits or transforms by default, what a reader may miss, and how to change the behavior.
records.use_when: Defaults filter, hide, or transform the output a reader expects to see.

records.title: Explain how to choose an update channel
records.summary: When multiple release streams are offered, state the differences in stability, update cadence, and what the reader should install.
records.use_when: The project publishes parallel release channels with different update expectations.

records.title: Explain what happens when a step is repeated
records.summary: State whether repeating a command converges on the same result, resumes work, or creates another copy.
records.use_when: A script or setup step may be run again on the same input.

records.title: Explain what uninstall removes and retains
records.summary: State which commands or files uninstall removes and what happens to data, configuration, caches, or installed components.
records.use_when: Uninstall removes a program and has separate effects on user data or settings.

records.title: Explain where project decisions are made
records.summary: Link a project’s governance and identify who makes major decisions.
records.use_when: Community proposals and final decisions happen in different places.

records.title: Expose discovery metadata through the README
records.summary: Use host-supported metadata for fields such as dataset language, license, tags, and file layout.
records.use_when: A host indexes documented machine-readable metadata in a README.

records.title: First successful result link
records.summary: Point to the file, page, or artifact the task created so it is easy to inspect.
records.use_when: The setup creates a file or page the reader can inspect directly.

records.title: Generate repetitive README sections from their source
records.summary: Generate sections such as configuration inputs or outputs from their authoritative definitions.
records.use_when: A README table, list, or example repeats facts maintained elsewhere.

records.title: Give a deprecation notice a replacement and timeline
records.summary: Name the affected interface, link the replacement or migration route, and distinguish the deprecation date from any planned retirement date.
records.use_when: A public command, API, or package is being retired in favor of another.

records.title: Give a readiness check before the first request
records.summary: After the startup command, show what indicates the dependency can accept traffic and how the reader can check it.
records.use_when: Process startup can finish before the service can accept work.

records.title: Give color-coded information a text label
records.summary: Label states, branches, or series in words when color conveys their meaning.
records.use_when: A screenshot, table, or chart uses color to convey meaning.

records.title: Give each public package its own README entry point
records.summary: Put a short orientation in the package directory so someone entering through a deep link can find its purpose, setup, and supporting docs.
records.use_when: A repository contains multiple independently used packages.

records.title: Give readers an upgrade preflight
records.summary: Link a compatibility check readers can run before an upgrade changes their existing installation.
records.use_when: Compatibility can be checked before an upgrade changes state.

records.title: Give service examples a sandbox route
records.summary: Name the sandbox or mock used by the example and state what effects it simulates.
records.use_when: The first service request should run without changing production state.

records.title: Guest or offline first run
records.summary: Offer a first-use path with minimal account or network dependencies when supported.
records.use_when: The first successful task can be done without connectivity or registration.

records.title: Guide readers through a pinned walkthrough with evidence
records.summary: Pair a task link and recognizable output with a pinned walkthrough and evidence of the checks that ran.

records.title: Human guide for a structured inventory
records.summary: Pair a machine-readable manifest with an explanation of its reader-facing purpose.
records.use_when: A structured inventory is easy for software to parse and lacks a human entry point.

records.title: Identify required assets distributed separately
records.summary: State which graphics, sound, models, or other runtime assets the checkout needs.
records.use_when: A clean checkout omits assets required for the first run.

records.title: Identify the source of truth when repositories are mirrored
records.summary: Name the canonical repository and explain which revision identifiers to cite from a mirror.
records.use_when: A mirror exposes code and directs decisions or contributions elsewhere.

records.title: Include a data dictionary for shared datasets
records.summary: Explain file relationships, field names, units, and missing-value codes so another person can interpret the data.
records.use_when: A dataset includes fields or values that are hard to interpret from names alone.

records.title: Independent version lines
records.summary: Name the product, README, or collection beside each version when their release lines differ.
records.use_when: A product, template, dataset, or docs set ships on its own release cadence.

records.title: Installation methods
records.summary: Distinguish packages, installers, source builds, and other supported options.
records.use_when: Readers can install through multiple supported channels.

records.title: Known limitations and workarounds
records.summary: State a known constraint and the currently supported path around it.
records.use_when: A known constraint blocks a reasonable workflow and a supported workaround exists.

records.title: Label ownership of installation channels
records.summary: Identify who maintains and supports each package or installer so readers know where to report installation problems.
records.use_when: Official and community installation channels coexist.

records.title: Label the scope of compatibility evidence
records.summary: State the version, platform, capability, and checks that support a compatibility claim.
records.use_when: A compatibility claim depends on a particular platform, version, or path through the workflow.

records.title: Language routing
records.summary: Link translated docs and make the expected language clear.
records.use_when: A README is maintained in multiple languages.

records.title: License and reuse link
records.summary: Point to the actual terms and distinguish project assets with different terms.
records.use_when: Code, documentation, data, or design assets may have distinct terms.

records.title: Lightweight link verification
records.summary: Check that critical relative targets and anchors resolve at the claimed revision.
records.use_when: Relative links, fragments, or evidence URLs can drift as files move.

records.title: Link a parts list for the hardware revision
records.summary: Give builders a bill of materials that matches the design they are assembling.
records.use_when: Hardware builds differ by revision, assembly variant, or optional part.

records.title: Link authoritative agent instructions
records.summary: Point an agent to the repository’s applicable instructions from the README.
records.use_when: An agent needs repository-specific editing or validation guidance before acting.

records.title: Link both a notebook preview and a runnable notebook
records.summary: Label the link for inspecting saved results and the link for launching the notebook at the corresponding revision.
records.use_when: A notebook has value both as readable output and as an executable walkthrough.

records.title: Link directly to a project-configured workspace
records.summary: Point readers to a preconfigured development workspace tied to the repository and intended branch.
records.use_when: The project can supply a known workspace configuration for first-time users.

records.title: Link the machine-readable interface contract
records.summary: Point to the specification or schema for the interface addressed by the README and identify its version.
records.use_when: A schema or contract is the authoritative definition for a versioned interface.

records.title: List the local service URLs by purpose
records.summary: When setup starts several services, tell readers which address opens the app, dashboard, API, or other local tool.
records.use_when: Several local services or ports become available during setup.

records.title: List what each format can read, write, and preserve
records.summary: Separate input and output support.
records.use_when: Import, export, or round-trip behavior varies by file format.

records.title: Live demo or playground
records.summary: Link directly to a usable experience and state access requirements.
records.use_when: A low-friction hosted example can show a useful first result.

records.title: Map application files by purpose
records.summary: List the locations for user data, configuration, runtime state, and cache on supported platforms.
records.use_when: Files have different persistence, cleanup, or migration needs.

records.title: Map each claim to the check that can reproduce it
records.summary: Pair the claim or reported result with its command, expected outcome, and the data it produces.
records.use_when: A release, paper, or benchmark makes several separately checkable claims.

records.title: Match firmware to the physical hardware revision
records.summary: Help readers identify the device revision and map it to the correct build or download target.
records.use_when: Firmware files look interchangeable and hardware compatibility differs.

records.title: Minimal working example
records.summary: Show the smallest realistic input and operation that demonstrate the capability.
records.use_when: A small standalone example can prove the core behavior.

records.title: Next action after success
records.summary: Offer a natural second task once the first one works.
records.use_when: The quickstart ends before a common next task.

records.title: Offer a smoke test and a full reproduction separately
records.summary: Use a small run to establish that setup works and a separate run to reproduce the full result.
records.use_when: The complete reproduction is too costly for a first setup check.

records.title: Offer an importable API request collection
records.summary: Link a reusable request collection so readers can run the same requests in their API client.
records.use_when: An API example has multiple requests or variables that a client can import.

records.title: Offer an isolated trial command
records.summary: Give the reader a short way to try a tool without installing it into their project.
records.use_when: A trial can be disposable while installation changes persistent state.

records.title: One prominent first action
records.summary: Lead with a recognizable task such as play, try, install, or adopt.
records.use_when: Several links compete for a new reader’s attention.

records.title: Pair the install name with the name used in code
records.summary: When distribution, import, or executable names differ, show the exact names together so readers can connect the installation step to the first use.
records.use_when: The package manager name differs from the executable or import identifier.

records.title: Permanent proof links
records.summary: Keep verification traceable with a commit-pinned receipt and recorded run, attempt, artifact ID, and digest.
records.use_when: A public claim needs evidence that can be traced back to the exact run and revision.

records.title: Prerequisite or installation check
records.summary: Show a fast way to check that the local environment is ready before the demo.
records.use_when: A short check can distinguish a ready installation from a missing prerequisite.

records.title: Prerequisites next to the task
records.summary: Name tools, versions, access, and prior setup before any commands depend on them.
records.use_when: A command assumes an installed tool, a credential, or a running service.

records.title: Preview changes before applying them
records.summary: When a workflow changes state and offers a preview, give the preview and apply steps distinct labels.
records.use_when: An operation can describe its planned changes before it applies them.

records.title: Progressive disclosure
records.summary: Collapse optional details or move them to a clearly labeled supporting document.
records.use_when: Optional detail interrupts the core reading path.

records.title: Project status and maturity
records.summary: Distinguish a preview, stable release, or archived project.
records.use_when: Preview, experimental, stable, or archived status changes adoption decisions.

records.title: Provide a starter control map
records.summary: List the actions a player needs in the first minute and map them to each supported input type.
records.use_when: A game or interactive demo needs input mappings before the first action.

records.title: Publication-path verification
records.summary: Test links and assets from the path where the README will actually ship.
records.use_when: Content is served from a publication surface distinct from its source file.

records.title: Published release link
records.summary: Give a direct path to the release named in the README and its release notes.
records.use_when: A reader needs the official published assets for a specific version.

records.title: Put a practice task before its worked solution
records.summary: When the README is also a learning guide, give readers a short task and a way to check their attempt.
records.use_when: A tutorial reader should practice a skill before seeing an answer.

records.title: Recognize contribution types beyond code
records.summary: Label what people contributed, such as documentation, design, translation, or testing, in the README or linked credits.
records.use_when: Help beyond code is welcome and needs recognizable entry points.

records.title: Recovery beside the failed step
records.summary: Put a common failure and its recovery close to the command or action that produces it.
records.use_when: A common failure occurs at a specific command or prerequisite.

records.title: Relative navigation
records.summary: Link same-checkout guides and assets with paths relative to the Markdown file.
records.use_when: A guide, example, or asset ships with the same checkout as its README.

records.title: Rendered review at two widths
records.summary: Check the landing page on wide and narrow layouts for overflow or unreadable content.
records.use_when: Wide tables, screenshots, or code blocks may be hard to use on narrow screens.

records.title: Reuse a README as the package listing
records.summary: Wire the maintained README into package metadata so package users see the same introduction in their registry.
records.use_when: The same README is consumed by a package or registry landing page.

records.title: Roadmap pointer
records.summary: Link planned work to a maintained roadmap and distinguish it from available features.
records.use_when: Readers need to distinguish current scope from future plans.

records.title: Route by reader task
records.summary: Give distinct reader goals clear routes from the same homepage.
records.use_when: Different readers arrive with different first tasks and need clear starting routes.

records.title: Route readers to editable designs and manufacturing exports
records.summary: Give separate links to the preferred files for modifying the design, files prepared for fabrication, and human-readable drawings where provided.
records.use_when: Designers and builders need different versions of the same design.

records.title: Safe configuration example
records.summary: Use labeled placeholders and explain where values belong.
records.use_when: Readers need a working configuration without including credentials or production defaults.

records.title: Sample fixture or starter input
records.summary: Provide a small known input that readers can use immediately.
records.use_when: Readers need input they can use immediately to reproduce an example.

records.title: Save or persistence checkpoint
records.summary: Tell readers what should survive a restart and how to confirm it.
records.use_when: The first task writes state that the reader expects to retain.

records.title: Scope boundaries
records.summary: Call out material limitations or environments outside the supported scope.
records.use_when: Readers could reasonably expect unsupported platforms or tasks to work.

records.title: Screenshot or result preview
records.summary: Show the key product screen or output readers should recognize.
records.use_when: The expected output or UI is easier to recognize visually.

records.title: Section deep links
records.summary: Send the reader to the relevant part of a guide and recheck anchors when headings change.
records.use_when: A specific subsection answers the reader’s question.

records.title: Security reporting route
records.summary: Link the project’s supported private disclosure process when applicable.
records.use_when: The project has a private channel for security reports.

records.title: Send readers to docs for their installed version
records.summary: Label stable and development docs links so readers can match them to the version they are using.
records.use_when: Instructions differ across supported installed releases.

records.title: Separate diagnostic capture from sharing
records.summary: Tell readers how to capture relevant evidence, where the resulting bundle lands, and how to inspect or anonymize it before sending it through the support route.
records.use_when: Support may ask for logs or a bundle containing local details.

records.title: Separate guide types
records.summary: Route readers to a tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation according to their task.
records.use_when: The project has material for learning, completing tasks, lookup, and background.

records.title: Separate platform commands
records.summary: Label POSIX and PowerShell paths where their commands differ.
records.use_when: Commands or syntax differ across supported operating systems or shells.

records.title: Set a time and cost expectation before setup
records.summary: State how long the example usually takes and whether it can create billable resources, with a link to current terms when pricing depends on an account or provider.
records.use_when: Installation time, disk, compute, or spend could affect whether a reader starts.

records.title: Show a benchmark case that changes the takeaway
records.summary: Beside a favorable result, include a reproducible workload or flag change that reduces the advantage or changes performance.
records.use_when: A benchmark advantage depends heavily on data or workload shape.

records.title: Show a recognizable first result
records.summary: Tell the reader what success looks like immediately after the first real task.
records.use_when: A quickstart produces output the reader must recognize before continuing.

records.title: Show a restore check against a separate destination
records.summary: Pair a backup path with a small restore exercise into a separate destination and show what to inspect in the restored copy.
records.use_when: The project stores important state and has a documented backup path.

records.title: Show configuration precedence
records.summary: Explain which setting wins when flags, environment variables, configuration files, and defaults disagree.
records.use_when: The same setting can be supplied in multiple places.

records.title: Show how another workflow consumes an output
records.summary: Document output names and show a caller reading one of those outputs.
records.use_when: A consumer uses a producer’s file, output value, or artifact.

records.title: Show how asset variants map to published files
records.summary: Give the file naming pattern, label the dimensions or styles that change the filename, and show where to check whether a combination exists.
records.use_when: Several published exports come from the same editable asset.

records.title: Show how to activate an installed extension
records.summary: Name the first command, view, or event that activates the extension and the behavior a reader should see.
records.use_when: An extension needs activation after installation.

records.title: Show how to enable optional capabilities
records.summary: Identify what the base install enables and which feature flag or package extra enables each optional capability.
records.use_when: An example requires features or dependencies excluded from the base installation.

records.title: Show how to prepare an offline install
records.summary: Separate gathering dependencies on a connected machine from installing the staged set on the offline target.
records.use_when: Installation targets cannot access the package registry during setup.

records.title: Show how to retrieve every page of results
records.summary: Give an example that spans multiple pages, follows the continuation link or cursor, and states when to stop.
records.use_when: A service limits result count or returns continuation tokens.

records.title: Show how to verify the artifact’s producer
records.summary: Where a release provides a signed attestation, show how to verify it against the expected repository or workflow.
records.use_when: Readers need to check who built an artifact and where it was built.

records.title: Show the order for upgrading multiple components
records.summary: When components evolve independently, show the upgrade sequence and which version combinations can coexist during the transition.
records.use_when: An upgrade crosses independently versioned services, nodes, or clients.

records.title: Show the permissions automation needs
records.summary: Name the caller permissions the example needs and what each one allows.
records.use_when: A workflow fails with defaults or requires deliberate access to perform a step.

records.title: Snapshot source identity
records.summary: Record the origin and digest of frozen README or asset bytes when exact archival identity matters.
records.use_when: A historical README or visual must be traceable to exact source bytes.

records.title: Starting directory and checkout
records.summary: State where commands begin and which revision or project root they expect.
records.use_when: A step depends on the checkout, subdirectory, or package root.

records.title: State the project’s purpose
records.summary: Tell a new reader what the project does and what they can accomplish with it.
records.use_when: A first-time reader needs to decide whether the project solves their problem.

records.title: State what event consumers can assume about delivery
records.summary: Say whether event delivery can repeat or arrive out of order and where to find the identifier needed to recognize a repeat.
records.use_when: A subscriber needs to handle duplicates, ordering changes, or retries.

records.title: State which saved data a release can open
records.summary: Name which older saves, archives, or project files the new version can read, and describe rollback separately where supported.
records.use_when: File compatibility differs across releases or file format versions.

records.title: Status badges
records.summary: Surface meaningful build, release, or license signals and link each badge to its source.
records.use_when: A visible workflow, package, or release signal can substantiate a specific current status.

records.title: Support and issue route
records.summary: Tell readers where to report a bug or ask for help and what evidence to include.
records.use_when: User questions, bugs, and other requests have different destinations.

records.title: Table of contents or jump links
records.summary: Expose major sections when the page is long enough to need them.
records.use_when: A long README has several independent tasks readers need to revisit.

records.title: Task-local help link
records.summary: Put the relevant support path beside a high-friction step.
records.use_when: Someone at a specific step needs a narrow reference or recovery path.

records.title: Text equivalent for a chart or diagram
records.summary: Put essential values, conclusions, or relationships in surrounding text.
records.use_when: A chart or diagram carries values, relationships, or trends used in the text.

records.title: Theme-aware images
records.summary: Check readability against light and dark backgrounds and provide variants when needed.
records.use_when: The same image loses contrast in one of the supported color themes.

records.title: Track the source revision of translations
records.summary: Link a translated README to its original and record which revision or release it follows.
records.use_when: Translations can be published or updated separately from the source language.

records.title: Turn an archived README into a handoff
records.summary: Put the maintained successor and new project name, if any, at the top of the archive.
records.use_when: An archived repo remains visible and readers need an onward route.

records.title: Turn examples into regression tests
records.summary: Generate test cases from examples in the maintained documentation source so changing an example also changes what gets tested.
records.use_when: An example can break when code, flags, or fixtures change.

records.title: Upgrade or migration route
records.summary: Name the starting version, intended destination, and relevant migration guide.
records.use_when: Existing installations or saved files need a defined path to a later release.

records.title: Use labeled callouts at the point of action
records.summary: Use short labeled notices for important context or consequences beside the relevant step.
records.use_when: A warning or note only matters for one specific action.

records.title: Value proposition
records.summary: Explain the practical payoff or problem the project removes.
records.use_when: The first paragraph names features and leaves their practical benefit implicit.

records.title: Verify which README appears on the repository homepage
records.summary: When multiple eligible README files exist, check which one the host surfaces and publish the expected content there.
records.use_when: More than one tracked README or ref could become the GitHub homepage.

records.title: Versioned section map
records.summary: Provide a path to find corresponding sections across archived READMEs.
records.use_when: Several maintained README editions organize the same tasks differently.

records.title: Write a copyable Quickstart
records.summary: Give readers ordered commands they can paste into the supported shell.
records.use_when: A reader can install, build, or run the project from a terminal.

records.title: Write image alternatives for their purpose
records.summary: Give informative, decorative, functional, and complex visuals the text treatment their roles require.
records.use_when: An image communicates information, provides a link, or decorates the README.
